n: Following the Lord’s direction in stages, Israel camped at Rephidim—where there was no water. Even following God’s lead can bring us to hard places.

f.g: a campsite near Sinai; location uncertain

n: The people quarreled with Moses, demanding water. Moses asks why they test the Lord—doubting His care after all He had done.
Thirst drove them to accuse Moses of bringing them out to kill them, their children, and animals.
Moses cried to the Lord: “What shall I do?” The people were nearly ready to stone him. Leaders need the Lord’s help too.
The Lord told Moses to go ahead of the people with some elders as witnesses, carrying the same staff that struck the Nile.

f.w: thy rod, wherewith thou smotest the river

n: God promised to stand before Moses on the rock at Horeb. When Moses struck it, water flowed. Paul taught that “that Rock was Christ,” the source of living water.
Moses named the place Massah (“testing”) and Meribah (“quarreling”), because the people asked, “Is the LORD among us, or not?”—despite His pillar of cloud overhead.
Then Amalek—descendants of Esau—attacked Israel. Deuteronomy says they struck the weak and weary at the rear.
Moses appoints Joshua to lead the fighting while Moses stands on the hill holding the rod of God. This is Joshua’s first appearance.

f.g: “Jehovah saves”; the Hebrew form of the name Jesus

n: Joshua fought, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur climbed the hilltop.

f.g: a leader of Judah, possibly grandfather of Bezalel the craftsman

n: When Moses raised his hands, Israel prevailed; when he lowered them, Amalek prevailed. Victory depended on reliance on God, symbolized by the uplifted hands.

f.g: perhaps in prayer, or holding the rod aloft

n: When Moses grew tired, Aaron and Hur sat him on a stone and held up his hands until sunset. A powerful picture of sustaining our leaders.
Joshua defeated Amalek’s army in battle.
The Lord commanded Moses to write this event in a book—one of the first mentions of writing scripture—and tell Joshua, because Amalek would one day be blotted out.

f.w: Write this for a memorial in a book

n: Moses built an altar named Jehovah-nissi, “The LORD is my banner”—the rallying flag around which Israel gathers.
The Hebrew here is difficult; it seems to say “a hand upon the throne (or banner) of the LORD.” The Lord vows ongoing war with Amalek because Amalek attacked His people.

f.g: Hebrew literally “a hand upon the throne of Yah”
